So I keep running into this at work, um, we have these huge folders of RAW photos from product shoots, and the naming is chaos, every photographer does their own thing. What I want is a command line tool, just something I can run like in the terminal, that scans a folder of images, reads the EXIF data, and renames everything to a consistent scheme, like date, shoot name, camera, sequence number. And it should detect duplicates too, like actual pixel duplicates not just same filename, because people copy files around and we end up with the same shot five times. Um, important thing, it has to do a dry run first, show me what it would rename before touching anything, I've been burned by tools that just go for it. And an undo, like it writes a little manifest so you can revert the last run. It needs to work on Windows and Mac because half the team is on each. Oh and it should be fast on like ten thousand files, not sit there for ten minutes. I'd want to ship it to the team as just one file they download, no installer, no runtime to install, they're photographers not developers. That's the whole thing really, it's a one person side project, I want it done in a couple weekends.
